name: Framing Effect
axiom: People decide differently when the same facts are described as gains rather than losses.
trigger: Two screens state one outcome, but one stresses what is gained and the other what is lost, and choices diverge.
checklist: State availability as uptime gained (99.9%) rather than downtime risk.
Present discounts as money saved rather than total billed.
Describe security work as protecting data rather than as a failure warning.

antiPattern.violation: A backup prompt warns that refusing leaves all records open to total loss.
antiPattern.remediation: The same prompt explains that enabling backup protects local files against hardware failure.

academicOrigin.title: The Framing of Decisions and the Psychology of Choice
